description: Every port either role listens on or dials. Overlay-only ports are unreachable from the WAN by design.

measurement.method: ss -ltnup, plus reading each named service's bind path
measurement.host: single peer, aarch64, no WireGuard kernel interface available
measurement.caveat: Runtime states are true of THIS host only. A port marked not-listening here may be running on a node with a live overlay. implementation_state is a property of the code and travels with the contract; runtime is a property of one machine and does not.

implementation_state.implemented: The code exists and binds the port it names.
implementation_state.provisioned: Scaffolding or config exists, but nothing binds the port yet.
implementation_state.spec-only: Designed and contracted, no code, by deliberate role boundary.

runtime.running: A listener was observed on this host at measurement time.
runtime.not-listening: No listener was observed on this host at measurement time.
runtime.not-verifiable-here: Cannot be observed from this host, because the interface it needs does not exist here.

51820.note: Carries the overlay itself. Reachable over the WAN because the Master must be dialled from behind NAT; peers behind NAT rely on PersistentKeepalive to keep the mapping open.
51820.runtime_why: Render script, systemd unit, config template and tests all exist (peer-node/scripts/sparknet-wireguard-render.sh, peer-node/systemd/sparknet-wireguard-anchor.service). The interface never comes up on this host: no wg binary, so wg0 does not exist and there is nothing to observe.

9090.binds_to: the peer's own overlay address only
9090.note: The guard binds 10.100.0.x, never 0.0.0.0. That is why a legitimate Master request arrives from 10.100.0.1 and off-overlay clients are rejected.
9090.runtime_why: The daemon refuses to listen without an overlay address (peer-node/services/sparknet-guard-d.py:709-711, standalone mode). With wg0 absent it correctly declines to bind rather than falling back to a wildcard. This is the code working, not code missing — the distinction the previous boolean could not express.

8090.note: Master ACL changes POST here to force immediate routing adjustment on peers.
8090.status: SPEC ONLY — no listener exists by role boundary, not by omission. Tracked in master-node/plans/MASTER_BUILD_PLAN.md Step 7.

4096.note: OpenAI-compatible local proxy routing to domain agent ports. Local-only by design: it injects the user environment profile, so it must not be exposed.
4096.status: PROVISIONED, no listener. peer-node/services/sparknet-dispatch-bridge.py is a 110-line CLI with no bind or serve code. Tracked in peer-node/PLAN.md Step 4.

4097.status: PROVISIONED, no listener. peer-node/agents/engineering/agent.py is a two-line placeholder that prints its identity. Tracked in peer-node/PLAN.md Step 4.

4098.status: PROVISIONED, no listener. peer-node/agents/cyber/agent.py is a two-line placeholder that prints its identity. Tracked in peer-node/PLAN.md Step 4.

4100.status: PROVISIONED, no listener. peer-node/agents/vault-curator/agent.py is a two-line placeholder that prints its identity. Tracked in peer-node/PLAN.md Step 5.

4200.note: The single opencode server. Exactly one process serves every session on the node, which is what makes a session survive a UI restart and lets conversation passing reference a live session by id rather than by replayed transcript. Local-only: it carries the whole node's session authority.
4200.status: SPEC ONLY — no listener. Tracked in peer-node/PLAN.md Step 4.

4201.binds_to: the peer's own overlay address only
4201.note: Receives share offers and countersigned share grants from a sibling peer. Overlay-only because every request here must arrive over the fabric, carrying a grant naming the sender's fingerprint.
4201.status: SPEC ONLY — no listener. Tracked in peer-node/PLAN.md Step 8.

4202.binds_to: the peer's own overlay address only
4202.note: Carries a handoff payload. Separate from share-intake so that granting conversation passing does not implicitly grant knowledge sharing: two ports, two independent grants.
4202.status: SPEC ONLY — no listener. Tracked in peer-node/PLAN.md Step 6.

4203.note: The Master ratifies or refuses a share. This is the 2 h clock's authority side. Peers enforce the deadline themselves, so an unreachable Master causes shares to expire, never to hang.
4203.status: SPEC ONLY — no listener, by the same role boundary that keeps the rest of the Master unbuilt. Tracked in master-node/plans/MASTER_BUILD_PLAN.md Step 10.

4210.note: Vote exchange for a master election. Carries signed votes only — never a registry entry and never an approval, so it is not an authority-plane message even though it decides who holds the operational key. Distinct from 4203 share-ratification so that electing a master and confirming a share stay separately gated.
4210.status: SPEC ONLY — no listener. Contracted in contracts/consensus-protocol.md; tracked in master-node/plans/MASTER_BUILD_PLAN.md Step 14.

8080.note: The Master's administrative page: Open WebUI plus an opencode terminal into this role's vault and plan. Reachable only from inside the overlay. This is the surface most worth attacking and the one with the most to lose, so it binds the overlay address and never a wildcard.
8080.admin_plane_not_authority_plane: Carries no signed authority message. A grant or approval originates at 4203/4210 and is signed in the isolated signer process, never here — which is why this port can be reachable by an LLM-driven multi-user surface at all.
8080.runtime_why: Committed declarative config exists (master-node/configs/admin-surface/docker-compose.admin.yml, master-node/configs/admin-surface/opencode.json) and the declared topology is asserted by master-node/tests/test_admin_surface.py, but Open WebUI is not installed on this host and no overlay interface exists, so nothing binds 8080. `provisioned` rather than `implemented`: config without a listener.
8080.status: PROVISIONED, NOT DEPLOYED — reachability is DoD: confirm: user in master-node/plans/MASTER_BUILD_PLAN.md Step 18. Tracked as a declared surface, not a running one.

4220.note: The fabric git server: authorized nodes clone, push and fetch the shared repository through the Master. The Master administers it — creates the repository, manages the authorized-key allowlist and activates the service.
4220.status: SPEC ONLY — no code and no daemon by design. Role responsibility contracted in master-node/docs/master-control-plane.md and scoped in master-node/plans/MASTER_ADMIN_PLAN.md.

4221.note: The fabric file sharing service: the Master hosts shared volumes that peers mount or fetch over the overlay. Separate from the per-peer 4201 share-intake grants because this is the infrastructure share, not a knowledge handoff between two peers.
4221.status: SPEC ONLY — no code and no daemon by design. Role responsibility contracted in master-node/docs/master-control-plane.md and scoped in master-node/plans/MASTER_ADMIN_PLAN.md.

4222.note: The Master's NAT administration surface for the overlay: peers behind NAT rely on the Master to keep mappings and routes coherent, complementing PersistentKeepalive on 51820. Listed as a control port; the NAT itself is data-plane behaviour, not a listener.
4222.status: SPEC ONLY — no code and no daemon by design. Role responsibility contracted in master-node/docs/master-control-plane.md and scoped in master-node/plans/MASTER_ADMIN_PLAN.md.

4223.note: The fabric vector embeddings database: a single store the roles and their wiki skills use for semantic retrieval, administered by the Master. Overlay-only because the index is cluster knowledge, not a public corpus.
4223.status: SPEC ONLY — no code and no daemon by design. Role responsibility contracted in master-node/docs/master-control-plane.md and scoped in master-node/plans/MASTER_ADMIN_PLAN.md.

invariants: No role binds a wildcard address for an overlay-only port.
Peer-side listeners that inject local identity or accept mutations stay off the overlay.
The Master binds 9090 nowhere; it dials peers on 9090.
implementation_state never claims implemented without a bind path in the named service.

A port may be implemented and simultaneously not-listening. That combination is the normal case for an overlay service on a host whose overlay is down, and it must not be collapsed into a single boolean.
runtime is measured per host and never published as a contract fact; only implementation_state travels.
